ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Explosive Plant Growth
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
EXPLOSIVE_GROWTH_RULED_REWRITE (design/RimMandrake/explosive_growth_ruled_spec_2026-10-16.md). Water decides how plants grow, and a watered native is a countdown.
Ships inside RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes as one of its engines (it has its own toggle on the Baroque Biomes settings page, and its own settings page). RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it.
ONE RATE PER PLANT, by its kind and its cell, multiplying its normal growth and only while it has light: dry-land natives x10 on wet ground and x0.1 on dry ground; jungle natives (Greentide, Miasma, Fever Wood, Webwork, Contagion) x4, wet or dry; anything yielding wood at 0.625 of its kind's rate; vanilla crops and plants x0.1 unless water lies within 2 cells (an option makes them normal); basins, pots and hydroponics at vanilla speed. A plant growing slower than normal also ages slower.
WET GROUND is ground with water on it, and only while it is there: rivers, fresh water, marsh and mud (their own cells), a flood (RimMandrake: Cracked Lands), spilled or poured water, a dug FlowWorks channel and the ground beside it, rain on open ground (and a few hours after, shown by puddles), snow in the biomes that say so, a salt-line surge's fresh side; fresh ash for fire-adapted plants. Clean water waters every plant; other liquids only plants adapted to them. Every fruiting plant uses the water on its cell.
WHERE. Only on maps whose biome Baroque Biomes ships; outside them our plants grow at vanilla speed (an UNSUPPORTED option applies the same rule elsewhere). A campaign layer's roster can put its whole world in scope (scopeAllBiomes).
THE CHARGE. A soaked plant that reaches full size keeps going: it swells past natural size, and it tells you, in a fixed order — the ground darkens, it swells, its hue shifts wrong, it trembles, it creaks, and then it goes silent. Then the top.
THE TOP belongs to the PLANT, never the ground it stands on: - The dry cycle (the default for dry-land natives): it fruits, throws many sprouts and dies; its seedlings carry the cycle on. One time in three it bursts instead. It respects your floors and walls. - The wet cycle (jungle natives): it fruits heavily, then withers, leaving a few sprouts. - A native sown as a crop drops its full harvest by itself, and its water is used up. - Burst (dry-adapted plants only): a pop, chaff, bruises and knockdown nearby (never lethal on its own), premium produce scattered — and a sown ring that ignores your zones, floors and doorways. - Tinder: a burst whose debris is fuel. - Slime: the ring turns the ground to slime. - Rupture (contaminated plants): a gas cloud, spawned things, sprouts, and mutations for anyone in the cloud without a full vacuum seal. - Flush (giant trees): it swells inside and survives, silently.
PLAYER VERBS. Harvest a swollen plant for extra produce. Cut it to defuse it — though once it trembles, the last swing is a gamble. Keep ground dry. Grazing animals (and a dry-air blower, where another mod ships one) suppress encroachment for a few days.
Every mechanic has a Mod Settings toggle; defaults are the shipped behaviour. Plant tops are data: an RM_ExplosiveGrowthRosterDef (by name, silently skipping absent plants) or an RM_ExplosiveGrowthExtension on a plant you own. Soak/suppress are exposed as RimMandrake.ExplosiveGrowth.ExplosiveGrowthAPI; the Baroque Biomes members (Cracked Lands, Environmental Hazards) call it directly, other mods may call it by reflection.
Ships the IncidentWorker behind a map-scale bloom (RM_IncidentWorker_BloomBurst); a campaign layer names the IncidentDef and the bloom plant.
The performance gate (TPS on a jungle-density map under a full-map soak) is OWED to a live session; no density is promised until it runs.
